151: 
152: @dataclass(frozen=True)
153: class Unit:
154:     scene: int
155:     fields: Tuple[Tuple[str, int], ...]  # probe / target / utterance
156: 
157:     def as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
158:         return dict(self.fields)
159: 
160: 
161: def trial_units(scenes: Sequence[Context], link: LinkLikelihood) -> List[Unit]:
162:     if link.name not in LinkLikelihood.CATEGORICAL:
163:         raise NotImplementedError(
164:             f"the design tool cannot score {link.name!r} ({link.response_type}) paradigms yet: its "
165:             f"responses are not categorical. Use choice, rating, production or binary_judgment.")
166:     units: List[Unit] = []
167:     games = set()
168:     for i, ctx in enumerate(scenes):
169:         if link.side == "speaker":  # a speaker's trial has no heard message: one unit set per game
170:             if ctx.objects in games:
171:                 continue
172:             games.add(ctx.objects)
173:         reps = sorted(set(ctx.choice_classes()))
174:         n_real = ctx.shape[1] - (1 if ctx.needs_sink else 0)
175:         if link.name == "choice":
176:             units.append(Unit(i, ()))
177:         elif link.name in ("rating", "ordered_beta"):
178:             units += [Unit(i, (("probe", r),)) for r in reps]
179:         elif link.name == "production":
180:             units += [Unit(i, (("target", r),)) for r in reps]
181:         elif link.name == "allocation":  # the whole split is the response: one unit per scene
182:             units.append(Unit(i, ()))
183:         else:
184:             units += [Unit(i, (("target", r), ("utterance", u))) for r in reps for u in range(n_real)]
185:     if len(units) > MAX_UNITS:
186:         raise ValueError(f"{len(units)} trial units, over the {MAX_UNITS} the EIG tool scores; narrow the "
187:                          f"scene_space (fewer or smaller sizes)")
188:     return units
189: 
190: 
191: def describe_unit(scenes: Sequence[Context], unit: Unit) -> Dict[str, Any]:
192:     ctx = scenes[unit.scene]
193:     return {"objects": [list(o) for o in ctx.objects], "heard": ctx.utterance, **unit.as_dict()}
194: 
195: 
196: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- outcome probabilities
197: 
198: def outcome_prob_draws(theory: TheoryModel, link: LinkLikelihood, theory_draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
199:                        link_draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray], scenes: Sequence[Context],
200:                        units: Sequence[Unit]) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
201:     """(draws, units, W) outcome probabilities and (units, W) valid outcome slots."""
202:     n_draws = len(next(iter(link_draws.values())))
203:     if theory_draws and len(next(iter(theory_draws.values()))) != n_draws:
204:         raise ValueError("theory and link draws must pair one to one")
205:     groups = group_by_shape(scenes)
206:     position = {}
207:     for group in groups.values():
208:         for pos, i in enumerate(group.indices):
209:             position[int(i)] = (group.shape, pos)
210:     by_group: Dict[Tuple[int, int], List[int]] = {}
211:     for u_idx, unit in enumerate(units):
212:         by_group.setdefault(position[unit.scene][0], []).append(u_idx)
213:     width = max(max(groups[s].shape) for s in by_group)  # outcome slots never exceed objects, messages, or points
214:     if link.name == "rating":
215:         width = max(width, link.options["scale_points"])
216:     if link.name == "ordered_beta":
217:         from src.rsa_open.links import slider_bin_edges
218: 
219:         width = max(width, len(slider_bin_edges(link.options["total_points"])) + 1)
220:     if link.name == "allocation":
221:         from src.rsa_open.links import bet_compositions, design_bet_total
222: 
223:         width = max(len(bet_compositions(n, design_bet_total(n, link.options["total_points"])))
224:                     for n in {s[0] for s in by_group})
225:     width = max(width, 2)
226:     probs = np.zeros((n_draws, len(units), width), dtype=np.float64)
227:     valid = np.zeros((len(units), width), dtype=bool)
228:     tp = {k: jnp.asarray(v) for k, v in theory_draws.items()}
229:     lp = {k: jnp.asarray(v) for k, v in link_draws.items()}
230:     for shape, unit_ids in by_group.items():
231:         group = groups[shape]
232:         latent = theory.latent_draws(tp, group, link.side == "speaker", n_draws)
233:         pos = np.asarray([position[units[u].scene][1] for u in unit_ids])
234:         arrays = jax.tree_util.tree_map(lambda a: a[pos], group.arrays)
235:         classes = jnp.asarray(group.classes[pos])
236:         keys = [k for k, _ in units[unit_ids[0]].fields]
237:         enc = {k: jnp.asarray([units[u].as_dict()[k] for u in unit_ids]) for k in keys}
238:         per_draw = jax.vmap(lambda lat, p: link.outcome_probs(lat, p, enc, arrays, classes))
239:         p = np.asarray(per_draw(latent[:, pos], lp), dtype=np.float64)
240:         v = np.asarray(link.outcome_valid(arrays, classes, enc))
241:         probs[:, unit_ids, :p.shape[2]] = p
242:         valid[unit_ids, :v.shape[1]] = v
243:     probs = np.where(valid[None], probs, 0.0)
244:     probs /= probs.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
245:     return probs, valid
246: 
247: 
248: def _link_draws(link: LinkLikelihood, n: int, seed: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
249:     keys = jax.random.split(jax.random.PRNGKey(seed), len(link.params))
250:     return {k: np.asarray(d.sample(key, (n,))) for (k, d), key in zip(link.params.items(), keys)}
251: 
252: 
253: def _theory_draws(draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray], n: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
254:     if not draws:  # a theory without parameters
255:         return {}
256:     total = len(next(iter(draws.values())))
257:     take = np.unique(np.linspace(0, total - 1, min(n, total)).round().astype(int))
258:     return {k: np.asarray(v)[take] for k, v in draws.items()}
259: 
260: 
261: def _score(ctx: DesignContext, scenes: Sequence[Context], link: LinkLikelihood, *, n_participants: int,
262:            trials_per_participant: int, distinct_trials: int, cost_usd: float, n_draws: int, n_scenarios: int,
263:            seed: int, lazy_full_every: Optional[int] = LAZY_FULL_EVERY) -> Dict[str, Any]:
264:     units = trial_units(scenes, link)
265:     if distinct_trials > len(units):
266:         raise ValueError(f"the design picks {distinct_trials} trial units but the scene space gives {len(units)}")
267:     responses = n_participants * trials_per_participant // distinct_trials
268:     per_setting = max(2, n_draws // LINK_SETTINGS)
269:     settings = _link_draws(link, LINK_SETTINGS, seed)  # one link setting per group, shared by every theory
270:     groups = np.repeat(np.arange(LINK_SETTINGS), per_setting)
271:     ld = {k: np.repeat(v, per_setting) for k, v in settings.items()}
272:     probs, valid = [], None
273:     for name in ctx.names:
274:         td = {k: np.tile(v, LINK_SETTINGS) for k, v in _theory_draws(ctx.draws[name], per_setting).items()}
275:         if td and len(next(iter(td.values()))) != len(groups):
276:             raise ContextInvalid(f"{name}: fewer than {per_setting} posterior draws")
277:         p, valid = outcome_prob_draws(ctx.theories[name], link, td, ld, scenes, units)
278:         probs.append(p)
279:     draw_groups = [groups] * len(probs)
280:     selection = eig.select(probs, valid, distinct_trials, n_responses=responses, prior=ctx.prior,
281:                            n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed, draw_groups=draw_groups,
282:                            lazy_full_every=lazy_full_every)
283:     (row,) = eig.power(probs, valid, selection.indices, [responses], prior=ctx.prior,
284:                        n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed + 1, names=ctx.names, draw_groups=draw_groups)
285:     return {
286:         "link": link.name, "n_units": len(units), "design_size": distinct_trials, "responses_per_unit": responses,
287:         "design": [{**describe_unit(scenes, units[i]), "source": src}
288:                    for i, src in zip(selection.indices, selection.sources)],
289:         "joint_eig_bits": row["joint_eig_bits"], "max_bits": row["max_bits"], "p_correct": row["p_correct"],
290:         "by_theory": row["by_model"], "cost_usd": cost_usd, "bits_per_dollar": row["joint_eig_bits"] / cost_usd,
291:     }
292: 
293: 
294: def reference_report(ctx: DesignContext, *, n_draws: int, n_scenarios: int, seed: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
295:     """The closed campaign's paradigm scored under the context's theories (cached in the context)."""
296:     from src.rsa.design_space import context_pool
297:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import BUDGET_USD
298: 
299:     key = f"reference_{ctx.sha256[:12]}_{n_draws}_{n_scenarios}_{seed}_lazy{LAZY_FULL_EVERY}.json"
300:     cached = ctx.root / key
301:     if cached.exists():
302:         return json.loads(cached.read_text())
303:     scenes = context_pool(REFERENCE["sizes"], include_prior_queries=REFERENCE["prior_queries"],
304:                           synonyms=REFERENCE["synonyms"])
305:     report = _score(ctx, scenes, likelihood(REFERENCE["link"]), n_participants=REFERENCE["n_participants"],
306:                     trials_per_participant=REFERENCE["trials_per_participant"],
307:                     distinct_trials=REFERENCE["distinct_trials"], cost_usd=BUDGET_USD, n_draws=n_draws,
308:                     n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed)
309:     report.pop("design")
310:     try:
311:         cached.write_text(json.dumps(report))
312:     except OSError:
313:         pass  # a read-only context (the designer's sandbox): the reference is recomputed, not lost
314:     return report
315: 
316: 
317: def score_paradigm(paradigm, ctx: DesignContext, *, n_draws: int = DEFAULT_DRAWS,
318:                    n_scenarios: int = DEFAULT_SCENARIOS, seed: int = 0, reference: bool = True,
319:                    reference_seed: int = 0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
320:     """The paradigm's design under the context's theories, its bits per dollar and the floor.
321: 
322:     The reference has a seed of its own (``reference_seed``), so every paradigm scored in one
323:     context meets the same floor, computed once (`reference_report`)."""
324:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import paradigm_likelihood, scene_pool
325: 
326:     d = paradigm.design
327:     report = {"paradigm_sha256": paradigm.sha256, "context_sha256": ctx.sha256, "theories": ctx.names,
328:               **_score(ctx, scene_pool(paradigm), paradigm_likelihood(paradigm),
329:                        n_participants=d.n_participants, trials_per_participant=d.trials_per_participant,
330:                        distinct_trials=d.distinct_trials, cost_usd=paradigm.cost_usd, n_draws=n_draws,
331:                        n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed),
332:               "settings": {"n_draws": n_draws, "n_scenarios": n_scenarios, "seed": seed}}
333:     if reference:
334:         ref = reference_report(ctx, n_draws=n_draws, n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=reference_seed)
335:         report["reference"] = ref
336:         report["floor_bits_per_dollar"] = FLOOR_SHARE * ref["bits_per_dollar"]
337:         report["meets_floor"] = bool(report["bits_per_dollar"] >= report["floor_bits_per_dollar"])
338:     return report
339: 
340: 
341: @dataclass
342: class Args:
343:     paradigm: Path
344:     context: Path
345:     out: Path
346:     n_draws: int = DEFAULT_DRAWS
347:     n_scenarios: int = DEFAULT_SCENARIOS
348:     seed: int = 0
349: 
350: 
351: def main(args: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
352:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import load_paradigm
353: 
354:     report = score_paradigm(load_paradigm(args.paradigm), load_context(args.context), n_draws=args.n_draws,
355:                             n_scenarios=args.n_scenarios, seed=args.seed)
356:     args.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
357:     print(f"{args.paradigm}: {report['joint_eig_bits']:.3f} of {report['max_bits']:.3f} bits, "
358:           f"${report['cost_usd']:.2f}, {report['bits_per_dollar']:.4f} bits/$ "
359:           f"(floor {report['floor_bits_per_dollar']:.4f}: {'meets' if report['meets_floor'] else 'BELOW'})")
360:     return report
361: 
362:

364:     main(tyro.cli(Args))

"""The designer's EIG tool (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §4): how much a paradigm would tell the live
theories apart, per dollar, and whether that clears the floor.

    uv run python -m src.rsa_open.design --paradigm paradigm.json --context <design context> --out report.json

**The design context** (`write_context`, `load_context`) is written by the harness and only read
by the designer: the live theories (``theories/<name>.py``), each theory's posterior draws on the
data so far (``draws/<name>.npz``, one array per parameter), and a uniform prior over the
theories (``context.json``). A context whose draws do not match its theories' parameters is
refused.

**Trial units** (`trial_units`) are the smallest things a design picks, for the paradigm's link:
a scene (choice); a scene and a probed object (rating); a scene and a target (production); a
scene, a target and a real message (binary judgment); a scene and a probed object (slider:
the ordered-beta link, its responses binned into 12 outcomes, so the score is a lower bound). A probe or target is taken once per class
of identical objects, since probing either gives the same predictions. A speaker's trial shows
no heard message, so its units are taken from the first scene of each game only. Bets (the allocation
link) are not categorical, and the tool refuses them (`NotImplementedError`) until it has an
estimator for them.

**Scoring** (`score_paradigm`): a new paradigm's link has no data yet, so its parameters are
drawn from the link's prior: ``LINK_SETTINGS`` settings, each paired with the same posterior
draws of every theory (``n_draws`` in all per theory). The outcome probabilities go to the
closed campaign's estimator (`src.rsa.design.eig`) with the draws grouped by link setting: a
scenario (a theory, one of its draws and simulated responses) compares the theories at its own
link setting. So the score is the information about the theories **given** the response
process, averaged over plausible response processes. Averaging over the link's prior inside
each theory's evidence instead (what the estimator does without groups) is a draw lottery:
with diffuse nuisance parameters and ~1,000 responses, a theory's evidence is whichever single
draw happens to fit, and a test on a rating paradigm picked the generating theory 72% of the
time at 32 draws, 91% at 256 and 100% with the link fixed, while reporting near-certainty
throughout. Links with more nuisance parameters would be scored worse, arbitrarily. The cost of
conditioning: a theory difference the link can mimic (a sharper listener vs a higher
temperature) counts as information here, though the joint fit may not separate it.

The design is a greedy joint-EIG selection of the paradigm's ``distinct_trials`` units, each
answered ``n_participants x trials_per_participant / distinct_trials`` times; its joint EIG and
power are then computed on fresh scenarios. The report gives the design, its bits, bits per
dollar, and the floor: ``FLOOR_SHARE`` of the bits per dollar of the closed campaign's
paradigm (`REFERENCE`) under the same theories (PI 2026-10-21). The reference is computed once
per context and settings and cached in the context when it is writable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import shutil
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
import tyro

from src.rsa.context import Context, group_by_shape
from src.rsa.design import eig
from src.rsa_open.fit import TheoryModel
from src.rsa_open.links import LinkLikelihood, likelihood

FLOOR_SHARE = 0.5
LINK_SETTINGS = 8
MAX_UNITS = 20_000
DEFAULT_DRAWS = 64
DEFAULT_SCENARIOS = 1000
# Lazy greedy (`src.rsa.design.eig.select`): a full pass every 16 picks, as main's design.
LAZY_FULL_EVERY = 16
# The closed campaign's paradigm: forced choice over the 1,597-display plain pool, 200 people
# answering 13 of 52 designed displays each, at the per-experiment budget.
REFERENCE = {"sizes": ((2, 2), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 2), (3, 3), (3, 4), (4, 2), (4, 3), (4, 4)),
             "prior_queries": True, "synonyms": True, "link": "choice",
             "n_participants": 200, "trials_per_participant": 13, "distinct_trials": 52}


class ContextInvalid(ValueError):
    """A design context that cannot be used."""


@dataclass
class DesignContext:
    root: Path
    theories: Dict[str, TheoryModel]
    draws: Dict[str, Dict[str, np.ndarray]]
    prior: np.ndarray
    sha256: str

    @property
    def names(self) -> List[str]:
        return list(self.theories)


def _sha(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def write_context(root: Path, theories: Mapping[str, Tuple[Path, Mapping[str, np.ndarray]]]) -> Path:
    """Write a design context: each theory's file and its posterior draws (param -> (draws,))."""
    root = Path(root)
    (root / "theories").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    (root / "draws").mkdir()
    record = {"theories": {}}
    for name, (path, draws) in theories.items():
        shutil.copyfile(path, root / "theories" / f"{name}.py")
        np.savez(root / "draws" / f"{name}.npz", **{k: np.asarray(v) for k, v in draws.items()})
        record["theories"][name] = {"theory_sha256": _sha(root / "theories" / f"{name}.py"),
                                    "draws_sha256": _sha(root / "draws" / f"{name}.npz")}
    (root / "context.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2))
    return root


def load_context(root: Path) -> DesignContext:
    root = Path(root)
    record_path = root / "context.json"
    if not record_path.exists():
        raise ContextInvalid(f"{root}: no context.json")
    record = json.loads(record_path.read_text())
    theories, draws, problems = {}, {}, []
    for name, shas in record["theories"].items():
        tpath, dpath = root / "theories" / f"{name}.py", root / "draws" / f"{name}.npz"
        if not tpath.exists() or not dpath.exists():
            problems.append(f"{name}: missing {tpath.name if not tpath.exists() else dpath.name}")
            continue
        if _sha(tpath) != shas["theory_sha256"] or _sha(dpath) != shas["draws_sha256"]:
            problems.append(f"{name}: its files changed since the context was written")
        theory = TheoryModel(tpath, name=name)
        with np.load(dpath) as d:
            arrays = {k: np.asarray(d[k]) for k in d.files}
        missing, extra = sorted(set(theory.params) - set(arrays)), sorted(set(arrays) - set(theory.params))
        if missing or extra:
            problems.append(f"{name}: draws lack {missing} / have extra {extra} (the theory's parameters are "
                            f"{list(theory.params)})")
            continue
        lengths = {len(v) for v in arrays.values()}
        if not theory.params:
            pass  # no parameters: nothing to draw
        elif len(lengths) != 1 or next(iter(lengths)) < 2:
            problems.append(f"{name}: every parameter needs the same number (>= 2) of draws; got {lengths}")
        elif not all(np.all(np.isfinite(v)) for v in arrays.values()):
            problems.append(f"{name}: draws are not all finite")
        theories[name], draws[name] = theory, arrays
    if problems:
        raise ContextInvalid(f"{root}:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {p}" for p in problems))
    if not theories:
        raise ContextInvalid(f"{root}: no theories")
    return DesignContext(root, theories, draws, np.full(len(theories), 1.0 / len(theories)), _sha(record_path))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- trial units

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Unit:
    scene: int
    fields: Tuple[Tuple[str, int], ...]  # probe / target / utterance

    def as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        return dict(self.fields)


def trial_units(scenes: Sequence[Context], link: LinkLikelihood) -> List[Unit]:
    if link.name not in LinkLikelihood.CATEGORICAL:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"the design tool cannot score {link.name!r} ({link.response_type}) paradigms yet: its "
            f"responses are not categorical. Use choice, rating, production or binary_judgment.")
    units: List[Unit] = []
    games = set()
    for i, ctx in enumerate(scenes):
        if link.side == "speaker":  # a speaker's trial has no heard message: one unit set per game
            if ctx.objects in games:
                continue
            games.add(ctx.objects)
        reps = sorted(set(ctx.choice_classes()))
        n_real = ctx.shape[1] - (1 if ctx.needs_sink else 0)
        if link.name == "choice":
            units.append(Unit(i, ()))
        elif link.name in ("rating", "ordered_beta"):
            units += [Unit(i, (("probe", r),)) for r in reps]
        elif link.name == "production":
            units += [Unit(i, (("target", r),)) for r in reps]
        elif link.name == "allocation":  # the whole split is the response: one unit per scene
            units.append(Unit(i, ()))
        else:
            units += [Unit(i, (("target", r), ("utterance", u))) for r in reps for u in range(n_real)]
    if len(units) > MAX_UNITS:
        raise ValueError(f"{len(units)} trial units, over the {MAX_UNITS} the EIG tool scores; narrow the "
                         f"scene_space (fewer or smaller sizes)")
    return units


def describe_unit(scenes: Sequence[Context], unit: Unit) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    ctx = scenes[unit.scene]
    return {"objects": [list(o) for o in ctx.objects], "heard": ctx.utterance, **unit.as_dict()}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- outcome probabilities

def outcome_prob_draws(theory: TheoryModel, link: LinkLikelihood, theory_draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
                       link_draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray], scenes: Sequence[Context],
                       units: Sequence[Unit]) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(draws, units, W) outcome probabilities and (units, W) valid outcome slots."""
    n_draws = len(next(iter(link_draws.values())))
    if theory_draws and len(next(iter(theory_draws.values()))) != n_draws:
        raise ValueError("theory and link draws must pair one to one")
    groups = group_by_shape(scenes)
    position = {}
    for group in groups.values():
        for pos, i in enumerate(group.indices):
            position[int(i)] = (group.shape, pos)
    by_group: Dict[Tuple[int, int], List[int]] = {}
    for u_idx, unit in enumerate(units):
        by_group.setdefault(position[unit.scene][0], []).append(u_idx)
    width = max(max(groups[s].shape) for s in by_group)  # outcome slots never exceed objects, messages, or points
    if link.name == "rating":
        width = max(width, link.options["scale_points"])
    if link.name == "ordered_beta":
        from src.rsa_open.links import slider_bin_edges

        width = max(width, len(slider_bin_edges(link.options["total_points"])) + 1)
    if link.name == "allocation":
        from src.rsa_open.links import bet_compositions, design_bet_total

        width = max(len(bet_compositions(n, design_bet_total(n, link.options["total_points"])))
                    for n in {s[0] for s in by_group})
    width = max(width, 2)
    probs = np.zeros((n_draws, len(units), width), dtype=np.float64)
    valid = np.zeros((len(units), width), dtype=bool)
    tp = {k: jnp.asarray(v) for k, v in theory_draws.items()}
    lp = {k: jnp.asarray(v) for k, v in link_draws.items()}
    for shape, unit_ids in by_group.items():
        group = groups[shape]
        latent = theory.latent_draws(tp, group, link.side == "speaker", n_draws)
        pos = np.asarray([position[units[u].scene][1] for u in unit_ids])
        arrays = jax.tree_util.tree_map(lambda a: a[pos], group.arrays)
        classes = jnp.asarray(group.classes[pos])
        keys = [k for k, _ in units[unit_ids[0]].fields]
        enc = {k: jnp.asarray([units[u].as_dict()[k] for u in unit_ids]) for k in keys}
        per_draw = jax.vmap(lambda lat, p: link.outcome_probs(lat, p, enc, arrays, classes))
        p = np.asarray(per_draw(latent[:, pos], lp), dtype=np.float64)
        v = np.asarray(link.outcome_valid(arrays, classes, enc))
        probs[:, unit_ids, :p.shape[2]] = p
        valid[unit_ids, :v.shape[1]] = v
    probs = np.where(valid[None], probs, 0.0)
    probs /= probs.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
    return probs, valid


def _link_draws(link: LinkLikelihood, n: int, seed: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    keys = jax.random.split(jax.random.PRNGKey(seed), len(link.params))
    return {k: np.asarray(d.sample(key, (n,))) for (k, d), key in zip(link.params.items(), keys)}


def _theory_draws(draws: Mapping[str, np.ndarray], n: int) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    if not draws:  # a theory without parameters
        return {}
    total = len(next(iter(draws.values())))
    take = np.unique(np.linspace(0, total - 1, min(n, total)).round().astype(int))
    return {k: np.asarray(v)[take] for k, v in draws.items()}


def _score(ctx: DesignContext, scenes: Sequence[Context], link: LinkLikelihood, *, n_participants: int,
           trials_per_participant: int, distinct_trials: int, cost_usd: float, n_draws: int, n_scenarios: int,
           seed: int, lazy_full_every: Optional[int] = LAZY_FULL_EVERY) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    units = trial_units(scenes, link)
    if distinct_trials > len(units):
        raise ValueError(f"the design picks {distinct_trials} trial units but the scene space gives {len(units)}")
    responses = n_participants * trials_per_participant // distinct_trials
    per_setting = max(2, n_draws // LINK_SETTINGS)
    settings = _link_draws(link, LINK_SETTINGS, seed)  # one link setting per group, shared by every theory
    groups = np.repeat(np.arange(LINK_SETTINGS), per_setting)
    ld = {k: np.repeat(v, per_setting) for k, v in settings.items()}
    probs, valid = [], None
    for name in ctx.names:
        td = {k: np.tile(v, LINK_SETTINGS) for k, v in _theory_draws(ctx.draws[name], per_setting).items()}
        if td and len(next(iter(td.values()))) != len(groups):
            raise ContextInvalid(f"{name}: fewer than {per_setting} posterior draws")
        p, valid = outcome_prob_draws(ctx.theories[name], link, td, ld, scenes, units)
        probs.append(p)
    draw_groups = [groups] * len(probs)
    selection = eig.select(probs, valid, distinct_trials, n_responses=responses, prior=ctx.prior,
                           n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed, draw_groups=draw_groups,
                           lazy_full_every=lazy_full_every)
    (row,) = eig.power(probs, valid, selection.indices, [responses], prior=ctx.prior,
                       n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed + 1, names=ctx.names, draw_groups=draw_groups)
    return {
        "link": link.name, "n_units": len(units), "design_size": distinct_trials, "responses_per_unit": responses,
        "design": [{**describe_unit(scenes, units[i]), "source": src}
                   for i, src in zip(selection.indices, selection.sources)],
        "joint_eig_bits": row["joint_eig_bits"], "max_bits": row["max_bits"], "p_correct": row["p_correct"],
        "by_theory": row["by_model"], "cost_usd": cost_usd, "bits_per_dollar": row["joint_eig_bits"] / cost_usd,
    }


def reference_report(ctx: DesignContext, *, n_draws: int, n_scenarios: int, seed: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The closed campaign's paradigm scored under the context's theories (cached in the context)."""
    from src.rsa.design_space import context_pool
    from src.rsa_open.paradigm import BUDGET_USD

    key = f"reference_{ctx.sha256[:12]}_{n_draws}_{n_scenarios}_{seed}_lazy{LAZY_FULL_EVERY}.json"
    cached = ctx.root / key
    if cached.exists():
        return json.loads(cached.read_text())
    scenes = context_pool(REFERENCE["sizes"], include_prior_queries=REFERENCE["prior_queries"],
                          synonyms=REFERENCE["synonyms"])
    report = _score(ctx, scenes, likelihood(REFERENCE["link"]), n_participants=REFERENCE["n_participants"],
                    trials_per_participant=REFERENCE["trials_per_participant"],
                    distinct_trials=REFERENCE["distinct_trials"], cost_usd=BUDGET_USD, n_draws=n_draws,
                    n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed)
    report.pop("design")
    try:
        cached.write_text(json.dumps(report))
    except OSError:
        pass  # a read-only context (the designer's sandbox): the reference is recomputed, not lost
    return report


def score_paradigm(paradigm, ctx: DesignContext, *, n_draws: int = DEFAULT_DRAWS,
                   n_scenarios: int = DEFAULT_SCENARIOS, seed: int = 0, reference: bool = True,
                   reference_seed: int = 0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The paradigm's design under the context's theories, its bits per dollar and the floor.

    The reference has a seed of its own (``reference_seed``), so every paradigm scored in one
    context meets the same floor, computed once (`reference_report`)."""
    from src.rsa_open.paradigm import paradigm_likelihood, scene_pool

    d = paradigm.design
    report = {"paradigm_sha256": paradigm.sha256, "context_sha256": ctx.sha256, "theories": ctx.names,
              **_score(ctx, scene_pool(paradigm), paradigm_likelihood(paradigm),
                       n_participants=d.n_participants, trials_per_participant=d.trials_per_participant,
                       distinct_trials=d.distinct_trials, cost_usd=paradigm.cost_usd, n_draws=n_draws,
                       n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=seed),
              "settings": {"n_draws": n_draws, "n_scenarios": n_scenarios, "seed": seed}}
    if reference:
        ref = reference_report(ctx, n_draws=n_draws, n_scenarios=n_scenarios, seed=reference_seed)
        report["reference"] = ref
        report["floor_bits_per_dollar"] = FLOOR_SHARE * ref["bits_per_dollar"]
        report["meets_floor"] = bool(report["bits_per_dollar"] >= report["floor_bits_per_dollar"])
    return report


@dataclass
class Args:
    paradigm: Path
    context: Path
    out: Path
    n_draws: int = DEFAULT_DRAWS
    n_scenarios: int = DEFAULT_SCENARIOS
    seed: int = 0


def main(args: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    from src.rsa_open.paradigm import load_paradigm

    report = score_paradigm(load_paradigm(args.paradigm), load_context(args.context), n_draws=args.n_draws,
                            n_scenarios=args.n_scenarios, seed=args.seed)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    print(f"{args.paradigm}: {report['joint_eig_bits']:.3f} of {report['max_bits']:.3f} bits, "
          f"${report['cost_usd']:.2f}, {report['bits_per_dollar']:.4f} bits/$ "
          f"(floor {report['floor_bits_per_dollar']:.4f}: {'meets' if report['meets_floor'] else 'BELOW'})")
    return report


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(tyro.cli(Args))

"""How long experiments take people (PI 2026-10-21): a digest for the designer's brief, and the
calibration of the pilot's time estimate, from the same records.

A designer must declare its paradigm's minutes, and the pilot gate checks them against an
estimate (`src.rsa_open.pilot`). The estimate's model (`model_seconds`: an overhead, reading at
``READING_WPM``, a look at each object and an answer per trial) is a guess; people's real times
correct it. Each `TimingRecord` is one finished experiment, as aggregates only: what people did
(response type, materials, trials, objects and words per trial, instruction length) and how
long they took (median, p10, p90 seconds, from Prolific's completion times or the page's own
clock). Two sources:
- **the closed campaign** (`CLOSED_CAMPAIGN`): its 9 live experiments, from the campaign
  reports (`docs/auto_rsa/CAMPAIGN_C*_REPORT.md`): 16 forced choices (13 + 2 catch + practice)
  on SVG displays averaging 3.44 objects. These are completion times only, never responses: the
  PI ruled that durations are not closed-campaign data in the sense of the drift rule (§5).
- **this campaign's finished experiments**, every chain's (`record_from_sessions`).

**Calibration** (`calibration`): the ratio of people's median to the model's estimate, as a
median over the records of the same response type when there are any, else over every record.
`estimated_minutes` is the model times that ratio; the record says which basis it used. With
the closed campaign alone, a choice paradigm's estimate is scaled by its own records, and any
other response type by the same choice records, until this campaign has run one of its kind.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from html import unescape
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import median
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Mapping, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

READING_WPM = 200
SECONDS_PER_OBJECT = 1.5
SECONDS_TO_ANSWER = {"choice": 2.0, "rating": 3.0, "slider": 4.0, "bet": 3.0, "production": 3.0,
                     "binary_judgment": 2.0}
SECONDS_PER_BET_OBJECT = 3.0
SECONDS_OVERHEAD = 30.0  # consent, page loads, the end screen


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TimingRecord:
    source: str
    response_type: str
    materials: str
    trials: int  # every trial a person answers: practice, test and catch
    objects_per_trial: float
    words_per_trial: float  # the prompt, and written objects for text materials
    instruction_words: int  # welcome, task and comprehension checks
    n_people: int
    median_s: float
    p10_s: float
    p90_s: float

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, d: Mapping[str, Any]) -> "TimingRecord":
        return cls(**d)


def _closed(chain: int, experiment: int, n: int, med: float, p10: float, p90: float) -> TimingRecord:
    # The closed page: 18 + 100 instruction words (welcome, "Meet Bob"); 24-word prompts.
    return TimingRecord(f"closed campaign, chain {chain}, experiment {experiment}", "choice", "svg", 16, 3.44,
                        24.0, 118, n, med, p10, p90)


# docs/auto_rsa/CAMPAIGN_C0_REPORT.md, CAMPAIGN_C1_REPORT.md, CAMPAIGN_C2_REPORT.md: completers.
CLOSED_CAMPAIGN: Tuple[TimingRecord, ...] = (
    _closed(0, 1, 200, 144, 86, 290), _closed(0, 2, 201, 124, 77, 200), _closed(0, 3, 201, 135, 85, 248),
    _closed(1, 1, 200, 119, 79, 212), _closed(1, 2, 201, 162, 96, 340), _closed(1, 3, 200, 126, 82, 242),
    _closed(2, 1, 196, 115, 74, 230), _closed(2, 2, 200, 129, 83, 254), _closed(2, 3, 200, 104, 69, 198),
)


def model_seconds(response_type: str, materials: str, trials: int, objects_per_trial: float,
                  words_per_trial: float, instruction_words: float) -> float:
    """The uncalibrated estimate of one person's time."""
    per_trial = (60.0 * words_per_trial / READING_WPM + SECONDS_PER_OBJECT * objects_per_trial
                 + SECONDS_TO_ANSWER[response_type]
                 + (SECONDS_PER_BET_OBJECT * objects_per_trial if response_type == "bet" else 0.0))
    return SECONDS_OVERHEAD + 60.0 * instruction_words / READING_WPM + trials * per_trial


def _words(s: str) -> int:
    return len(unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s)).split())


def features(lists: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """What a person does under these trial lists (averaged over the lists), for the model."""
    intro = lists["intro"]
    instruction = _words(intro["welcome"]) + _words(intro["task"]) + sum(
        _words(c["question"]) + sum(_words(o) for o in c["options"]) for c in intro["checks"])
    trials = [t for lst in lists["lists"] for t in lst["trials"]]
    text = lists["materials_kind"] == "text"
    words = [_words(t["prompt_html"]) + (sum(len(x.split()) for x in t["item_labels"]) if text else 0)
             for t in trials]
    return {"response_type": lists["response_type"], "materials": lists["materials_kind"],
            "trials": len(lists["lists"][0]["trials"]),
            "objects_per_trial": sum(len(t["objects"]) for t in trials) / len(trials),
            "words_per_trial": sum(words) / len(words), "instruction_words": instruction}


def calibration(records: Sequence[TimingRecord], response_type: str) -> Tuple[float, str]:
    """(people's median / the model's estimate, the basis), over records of this type if any."""
    def ratio(r: TimingRecord) -> float:
        return r.median_s / model_seconds(r.response_type, r.materials, r.trials, r.objects_per_trial,
                                          r.words_per_trial, r.instruction_words)

    same = [r for r in records if r.response_type == response_type]
    use = same or list(records)
    if not use:
        return 1.0, "no timing records: the model's estimate, uncalibrated"
    basis = (f"{len(use)} {response_type} experiment(s)" if same
             else f"{len(use)} experiment(s) of other response types (none of {response_type} yet)")
    return float(median(ratio(r) for r in use)), basis


def estimate(lists: Mapping[str, Any], records: Sequence[TimingRecord]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The calibrated estimate of a person's minutes under these lists, with how it was made."""
    f = features(lists)
    raw = model_seconds(**f) / 60.0
    k, basis = calibration(records, f["response_type"])
    return {"estimated_minutes": raw * k, "model_minutes": raw, "calibration": k, "calibration_basis": basis,
            **{f"features_{key}": value for key, value in f.items()}}


def record_from_sessions(source: str, lists: Mapping[str, Any], seconds: Sequence[float]) -> TimingRecord:
    """A finished experiment's record: its lists' features and its people's completion times."""
    if not seconds:
        raise ValueError(f"{source}: no completion times")
    s = sorted(float(x) for x in seconds)

    def q(p: float) -> float:
        return s[min(len(s) - 1, max(0, round(p * (len(s) - 1))))]

    f = features(lists)
    return TimingRecord(source, f["response_type"], f["materials"], f["trials"], round(f["objects_per_trial"], 2),
                        round(f["words_per_trial"], 1), f["instruction_words"], len(s), q(0.5), q(0.1), q(0.9))


def write_records(path: Path, records: Iterable[TimingRecord]) -> None:
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps([asdict(r) for r in records], indent=2))


def read_records(path: Path) -> List[TimingRecord]:
    return [TimingRecord.from_json(d) for d in json.loads(Path(path).read_text())]


def digest_md(records: Sequence[TimingRecord]) -> str:
    """The records as the designer reads them."""
    lines = ["# How long experiments took people", "",

             "| experiment | response | materials | trials | objects/trial | words/trial | people | median | "
             "p10-p90 | seconds/trial (median) |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in records:
        per_trial = (r.median_s - SECONDS_OVERHEAD - 60.0 * r.instruction_words / READING_WPM) / r.trials
        lines.append(f"| {r.source} | {r.response_type} | {r.materials} | {r.trials} | {r.objects_per_trial:g} | "
                     f"{r.words_per_trial:g} | {r.n_people} | {r.median_s / 60:.1f} min | "
                     f"{r.p10_s / 60:.1f}-{r.p90_s / 60:.1f} min | {per_trial:.1f} |")
    lines += ["", "Seconds per trial: the median, less a 30 s overhead and the instructions' reading time, "
              "over the trials. Prolific pays by the minutes you declare: declare about the median.", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)

1: """The paradigm spec the designer writes, and its validator (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3, §4, §8).
2: 
3: A paradigm is one JSON file: what the experiment asks (the charter question), its
4: instructions and comprehension checks, its materials (SVG or text only), the space of scenes
5: its trials are drawn from, the response type and the link that scores it, and the design (N,
6: trials, length, pay). Every trial maps onto an abstract scene, a `src.rsa.context.Context`:
7: referents with features and a heard message or none. Theories see only those scenes.
8: 
9: `load_paradigm` validates a spec and raises `ParadigmInvalid` listing **every** problem at once,
10: so an agent fixing a spec sees them all. It checks:
11: - structure and types, with unknown keys refused (a typo fails loudly);
12: - the design against the campaign's bounds: the closed campaign's budget per experiment
13:   (`BUDGET_USD`), at least `MIN_PARTICIPANTS`, at most `MAX_MINUTES` per person, and pay at the
14:   closed campaign's hourly rate (`MIN_HOURLY_USD`);
15: - the scene space: at most `MAX_OBJECTS` objects and `MAX_FEATURES` features, and at most
16:   `MAX_POOL` scenes (the EIG tools score every one);
17: - materials: every domain names enough features for the largest scene; SVG is well-formed and
18:   contains only drawing elements (no script, foreignObject, images, links, styles, event
19:   handlers, or references outside the fragment); text materials give each feature a phrase;
20: - content (PI 2026-10-20): no deception, no affectively charged stimuli or language, no URLs
21:   or email addresses;
22: - the response's link exists in the library (`src.rsa_open.links`) and scores its type; a
23:   rating gives its scale points and a slider its total points.
24: 
25: A paradigm's `sha256` is that of its canonical JSON, so formatting does not change it and any
26: content does; it is recorded with every trial collected under the paradigm.
27: 
28:     python -m src.rsa_open.paradigm --spec paradigm.json
29:     python -m src.rsa_open.paradigm --schema-out schema.json   # the JSON schema, for the designer

433:         spec = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
434:     except json.JSONDecodeError as err:
435:         raise ParadigmInvalid(str(path), [f"not valid JSON ({err})"]) from None
436:     return parse_paradigm(spec, str(path))
437: 
438: 
439: def scene_pool(paradigm: Paradigm) -> list:
440:     """The abstract scenes the paradigm's trials can show (`src.rsa.context.Context`)."""
441:     from src.rsa.design_space import context_pool
442: 
443:     return context_pool([tuple(s) for s in paradigm.scene_space.sizes],
444:                         include_prior_queries=paradigm.scene_space.prior_queries,
445:                         synonyms=paradigm.scene_space.synonyms)
446: 
447: 
448: def paradigm_likelihood(paradigm: Paradigm):
449:     """The paradigm's link likelihood, with its frozen options (`src.rsa_open.links`)."""
450:     from src.rsa_open.links import likelihood
451: 
452:     return likelihood(paradigm.response.link, scale_points=paradigm.response.scale_points,
453:                       total_points=paradigm.response.total_points)
454: 
455: 
456: def main_schema(out: Path) -> dict:
457:     schema = Paradigm.model_json_schema()
458:     Path(out).write_text(json.dumps(schema, indent=2))
459:     return schema
460: 
461: 
462: @dataclass
463: class Args:
464:     spec: Optional[Path] = None
465:     """A paradigm spec to validate."""
466:     schema_out: Optional[Path] = None
467:     """Write the spec's JSON schema here."""
468: 
469: 
470: def main(args: Args) -> None:
471:     if args.spec is None and args.schema_out is None:
472:         raise SystemExit("give --spec and/or --schema-out")
473:     if args.schema_out is not None:
474:         main_schema(args.schema_out)
475:         print(f"schema -> {args.schema_out}")
476:     if args.spec is not None:
477:         p = load_paradigm(args.spec)
478:         print(f"{args.spec}: valid. {len(scene_pool(p))} scenes; {p.response.type} via link {p.response.link!r}; "
479:               f"N={p.design.n_participants}, {p.design.minutes:g} min, ${p.cost_usd:.2f}; sha256 {p.sha256}")

"""The paradigm spec the designer writes, and its validator (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3, §4, §8).

A paradigm is one JSON file: what the experiment asks (the charter question), its
instructions and comprehension checks, its materials (SVG or text only), the space of scenes
its trials are drawn from, the response type and the link that scores it, and the design (N,
trials, length, pay). Every trial maps onto an abstract scene, a `src.rsa.context.Context`:
referents with features and a heard message or none. Theories see only those scenes.

`load_paradigm` validates a spec and raises `ParadigmInvalid` listing **every** problem at once,
so an agent fixing a spec sees them all. It checks:
- structure and types, with unknown keys refused (a typo fails loudly);
- the design against the campaign's bounds: the closed campaign's budget per experiment
  (`BUDGET_USD`), at least `MIN_PARTICIPANTS`, at most `MAX_MINUTES` per person, and pay at the
  closed campaign's hourly rate (`MIN_HOURLY_USD`);
- the scene space: at most `MAX_OBJECTS` objects and `MAX_FEATURES` features, and at most
  `MAX_POOL` scenes (the EIG tools score every one);
- materials: every domain names enough features for the largest scene; SVG is well-formed and
  contains only drawing elements (no script, foreignObject, images, links, styles, event
  handlers, or references outside the fragment); text materials give each feature a phrase;
- content (PI 2026-10-20): no deception, no affectively charged stimuli or language, no URLs

1: """The simulated pilot (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §4): LLM participants take a paradigm's trial
2: lists screen by screen, and the pilot gate decides whether the paradigm may go live.
3: 
4:     uv run python -m src.rsa_open.pilot --paradigm p.json --lists lists.json --out pilot/
5: 
6: **Participants** are Gemini 3.8 Flash (PI 2026-10-21, `PILOT_MODEL`), one chat per participant.
7: They see what the page shows (`src.rsa_open.screens`): the welcome and instructions, each
8: comprehension check (a wrong answer shows the instructions once more, as the page does), the
9: practice trial and every trial of one list, in order. A trial with SVG materials is shown as one
10: image of its objects, left to right, the marked one in an orange frame (rendered with resvg);
11: text materials are written out. Each screen asks for a reply line ``ANSWER: ...`` in the form
12: its widget takes (an object number, a rating, a slider value, points per object, a word, yes or
13: no); an unreadable reply is asked once more, then recorded as unreadable.
14: 
15: **The gate** (`gate`): a paradigm passes when
16: - comprehension: at least ``FLOORS['comprehension']`` of participants answer every check right
17:   by their second reading of the instructions;
18: - attention: at least ``FLOORS['catch']`` of catch trials are passed (`screens.catch_passed`);
19: - readability: at least ``FLOORS['readable']`` of trials get a usable answer;
20: - the test responses parse as the paradigm's link's data (`src.rsa_open.fit.OpenData.build`);
21: - the time estimate (`estimated_minutes`: `src.rsa_open.timing`'s model, calibrated on people's
22:   real times in finished experiments) is within ``TIME_TOLERANCE`` of the declared minutes;
23: - the test answers are not all one answer;
24: - legibility (SVG materials, `materials_check`): ``LEGIBILITY_CHECKERS`` fresh chats name each
25:   domain's base freely (a name other than the domain's goes to a judge chat: "is 'box' a
26:   reasonable name for robots?"), pick which of the domain's words names the part a single
27:   feature adds, and say exactly which objects of ``TRUTH_ITEMS`` real test trials a word is true
28:   of; at least ``FLOORS['legibility']`` of answers are right, and no feature or trial is misread
29:   by half of them or more (PI 2026-10-21: the first designer drew a bare box for a featureless
30:   robot, and a multiple-choice naming question passed it by elimination). A base named otherwise
31:   by half or more counts against the rate but alone is a warning, not a failure (PI 2026-10-21:
32:   a plain badge is fairly called a circle; the features and the words' truth carry the
33:   inference).
34: LLM participants are not people: the pilot finds instructions, prompts and materials that a
35: capable reader cannot follow, and data that do not parse; it says nothing about effect sizes.
36: """
37: 
38: from __future__ import annotations
39: 
40: import html
41: import json
42: import re
43: import time
44: from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
45: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
46: from pathlib import Path
47: from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Mapping, Optional, Protocol, Sequence, Tuple
48: 
49: import tyro
50: 
51: PILOT_MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash"
52: PILOT_PARTICIPANTS = 12
53: FLOORS = {"comprehension": 0.8, "catch": 0.8, "readable": 0.95, "legibility": 0.9}
54: LEGIBILITY_CHECKERS = 3
55: CHOICE_ASK = "Reply ANSWER: <the number of your choice>."
56: NAME_ASK = "Reply ANSWER: <your name for it>."
57: TRUTH_ASK = "Reply ANSWER: <their numbers, separated by commas>, or ANSWER: none."
58: TRUTH_ITEMS = 6
59: TIME_TOLERANCE = 0.30
60: SYSTEM = ("You are taking part in an online research study. Read each screen carefully and respond as a "
61:           "thoughtful participant would. End every reply with one line of the form `ANSWER: ...`, in the "
62:           "format the screen asks for.")
63: IMAGE_DROPPED = "(The picture shown with this screen is no longer shown.)"
64: ANSWER = re.compile(r"ANSWER:\s*(.+)", re.IGNORECASE)
65: FRAME, MARK = "#d7dbe1", "#d9822b"
66: 
67: 
68: class Participant(Protocol):
69:     name: str
70: 
71:     def reply(self, text: str, images: Sequence[bytes] = ()) -> str:
72:         """Send one screen (text and images) in this participant's conversation; their reply."""
73: 
74: 
75: class GeminiParticipant:
76:     """One conversation with a Gemini model; usage is recorded per call (`src.runtime.token_usage`).
77: 
78:     Only the current screen's picture is sent: an earlier turn keeps its words and the reply,
79:     with ``IMAGE_DROPPED`` where its picture was. A chat that resent every earlier picture made
80:     each call's input grow with the trial count (a 3-person pilot: 4.1M input tokens for 195
81:     calls); a person, too, remembers the task, not every earlier screen."""
82: 
83:     def __init__(self, model: str = PILOT_MODEL, temperature: float = 1.0, retries: int = 3, client=None):
84:         from google.genai import types
85: 
86:         self.name, self._types, self.retries = model, types, retries
87:         if client is None:
88:             from google import genai
89: 
90:             from src.pipelines.outer_loop.llm import resolve_google_api_key
91: 
92:             client = genai.Client(api_key=resolve_google_api_key(require=True))
93:         # Held: a client nothing refers to is closed when collected, under its calls.
94:         self._client = client
95:         self._config = types.GenerateContentConfig(system_instruction=SYSTEM, temperature=temperature)
96:         self._history: List[Any] = []
97: 
98:     def reply(self, text: str, images: Sequence[bytes] = ()) -> str:
99:         from src.runtime.token_usage import record_usage
100: 
101:         t = self._types
102:         pictures = [t.Part.from_bytes(data=png, mime_type="image/png") for png in images]
103:         turn = t.Content(role="user", parts=pictures + [t.Part.from_text(text=text)])
104:         for attempt in range(self.retries):
105:             try:
106:                 response = self._client.models.generate_content(model=self.name, contents=self._history + [turn],
107:                                                                 config=self._config)
108:                 break
109:             except Exception as err:  # an API error is the run's, not the paradigm's
110:                 if attempt == self.retries - 1:
111:                     raise RuntimeError(f"{self.name}: the pilot participant's API call failed: {err}") from err
112:                 time.sleep(2 ** (attempt + 1))
113:         usage = getattr(response, "usage_metadata", None)
114:         if usage is None:
115:             record_usage(source="rsa_open:pilot", backend="google-genai", model=self.name, usage_missing=True)
116:         else:
117:             record_usage(source="rsa_open:pilot", backend="google-genai", model=self.name,
118:                          input_tokens=int(usage.prompt_token_count or 0),
119:                          output_tokens=int(usage.candidates_token_count or 0),
120:                          reasoning_tokens=int(getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0))
121:         answer = response.text or ""
122:         kept = [t.Part.from_text(text=text)] + ([t.Part.from_text(text=IMAGE_DROPPED)] if images else [])
123:         self._history += [t.Content(role="user", parts=kept), t.Content(role="model", parts=[t.Part.from_text(text=answer)])]
124:         return answer
125: 
126: 
127: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- screens as text
128: 
129: def _plain(fragment: str) -> str:
130:     return html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", fragment)).strip()
131: 
132: 
133: def screen_png(trial: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bytes:
134:     """One image of an SVG trial's objects, left to right, the marked one framed in orange."""
135:     return row_png(trial["items_html"], trial["widget"].get("marked"))
136: 
137: 
138: def row_png(items_html: Sequence[str], marked: Optional[int] = None) -> bytes:
139:     """SVG objects drawn in a row of cards, as the page shows them."""
140:     import resvg_py
141: 
142:     cells = []
143:     for p, item in enumerate(items_html):
144:         inner = re.sub(r"^<svg[^>]*>", "", item)
145:         inner = inner[: inner.rfind("</svg>")]
146:         x = 10 + p * 120
147:         stroke, width = (MARK, 6) if p == marked else (FRAME, 3)
148:         cells.append(f'<rect x="{x - 4}" y="6" width="108" height="108" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" '
149:                      f'stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="{width}"/>'
150:                      f'<svg x="{x}" y="10" width="100" height="100" viewBox="0 0 100 100">{inner}</svg>')
151:     w = 20 + 120 * len(cells)
152:     svg = (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="120" viewBox="0 0 {w} 120">'
153:            f'<rect width="{w}" height="120" fill="#f3f4f6"/>{"".join(cells)}</svg>')
154:     return bytes(resvg_py.svg_to_bytes(svg_string=svg, zoom=2))
155: 
156: 
157: def trial_screen(trial: Mapping[str, Any], kind: str) -> Tuple[str, List[bytes]]:
158:     """A trial as the participant reads it: text, and its image for SVG materials."""
159:     w, n = trial["widget"], len(trial["items_html"])
160:     lines = ["(Practice question.)"] if trial["phase"] == "practice" else []
161:     lines.append(_plain(trial["prompt_html"]))
162:     images: List[bytes] = []
163:     if kind == "svg":
164:         images.append(screen_png(trial))
165:         lines.append(f"The picture shows {n} objects, numbered 1 to {n} from left to right.")
166:     else:
167:         lines += [f"Object {p + 1}: {label}" for p, label in enumerate(trial["item_labels"])]
168:     if w.get("marked") is not None:
169:         frame = "with an orange frame" if kind == "svg" else "marked"
170:         lines.append(f"The question is about object {w['marked'] + 1}, which is {frame}.")
171:     t = w["type"]
172:     if t == "choice":
173:         lines.append(f"Choose one object: reply ANSWER: <the object's number, 1 to {n}>.")
174:     elif t == "rating":
175:         lo, hi = w["labels"]
176:         lines.append(f"Answer on a scale from 1 ({lo}) to {w['points']} ({hi}): reply ANSWER: <1 to {w['points']}>.")
177:     elif t == "slider":
178:         lo, hi = w["labels"]
179:         lines.append(f"Set a slider from 0 ({lo}) to {w['max']} ({hi}): reply ANSWER: <a whole number, 0 to {w['max']}>.")
180:     elif t == "bet":
181:         lines.append(f"Split {w['total']} points among the objects: reply ANSWER: <{n} whole numbers, one per object "
182:                      f"in order, separated by commas, adding up to {w['total']}>.")
183:     elif t == "production":
184:         words = ", ".join(o["label"] for o in w["options"])
185:         lines.append(f"Choose one of these words: {words}. Reply ANSWER: <the word>.")
186:     else:
187:         lines.append("Reply ANSWER: yes or ANSWER: no.")
188:     return "\n".join(lines), images
189: 
190: 
191: def parse_answer(trial: Mapping[str, Any], reply: str) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], str]:
192:     """The response the page would record for this reply, or (None, why not)."""
193:     found = ANSWER.findall(reply)
194:     if not found:
195:         return None, "no line starting with ANSWER:"
196:     a = found[-1].strip().strip("`*").strip().rstrip(".")
197:     w, n = trial["widget"], len(trial["items_html"])
198:     order = trial["display_order"]
199:     t = w["type"]
200:     try:
201:         if t == "choice":
202:             k = int(a)
203:             if not 1 <= k <= n:
204:                 return None, f"the object number must be 1 to {n}"
205:             return {"choice": order[k - 1]}, ""
206:         if t == "rating":
207:             v = int(a)
208:             if not 1 <= v <= w["points"]:
209:                 return None, f"the rating must be 1 to {w['points']}"
210:             return {"probe": trial["probe"], "rating": v}, ""
211:         if t == "slider":
212:             v = int(a)
213:             if not 0 <= v <= w["max"]:
214:                 return None, f"the value must be 0 to {w['max']}"
215:             return {"probe": trial["probe"], "value": v}, ""
216:         if t == "bet":
217:             pts = [int(x) for x in re.split(r"[,\s]+", a) if x]
218:             if len(pts) != n or any(x < 0 for x in pts) or sum(pts) != w["total"]:
219:                 return None, f"give {n} non-negative whole numbers adding up to {w['total']}"
220:             by_object = [0] * n
221:             for p, x in enumerate(pts):
222:                 by_object[order[p]] = x
223:             return {"points": by_object}, ""
224:         if t == "production":
225:             words = {o["label"].lower(): o["utterance"] for o in w["options"]}
226:             word = a.strip("\"'“”").lower()
227:             if word not in words:
228:                 return None, f"the word must be one of {', '.join(o['label'] for o in w['options'])}"
229:             return {"target": trial["target"], "utterance": words[word]}, ""
230:         if a.lower() in ("yes", "no"):
231:             return {"target": trial["target"], "utterance": trial["utterance"], "answer": a.lower() == "yes"}, ""
232:         return None, "answer yes or no"
233:     except ValueError:
234:         return None, "the answer is not in the form asked for"
235: 
236: 
237: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- legibility
238: 
239: @dataclass(frozen=True)
240: class LegibilityItem:
241:     """One question about the materials (`legibility_items`)."""
242: 
243:     key: str  # "houses: the base" / "houses: chimney" / "trial 3: chimney"
244:     kind: str  # "name": free naming; "choice": one of ``options``; "truth": the objects a word is true of
245:     text: str
246:     image: bytes
247:     expected: Any  # the domain's name; the right option; the set of object numbers
248:     options: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
249: 
250: 
251: def _plural_key(word: str) -> str:
252:     w = word.strip().lower().strip("\"'“”.!")
253:     for suffix in ("ies", "es", "s"):
254:         if w.endswith(suffix) and len(w) > len(suffix) + 2:
255:             return w[: -len(suffix)] + ("y" if suffix == "ies" else "")
256:     return w
257: 
258: 
259: def legibility_items(paradigm, lists: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, seed: int = 0) -> List[LegibilityItem]:
260:     """The materials check's questions (SVG materials; text materials say what they are):
261: 
262:     - each domain's base alone, named freely ("name");
263:     - the base beside the base with one feature, which of the domain's words names the added part
264:       ("choice");
265:     - with ``lists``, up to ``TRUTH_ITEMS`` real test trials, unmarked: which objects have a word
266:       true of some but not all of them ("truth", exact)."""
267:     import numpy as np
268: 
269:     from src.rsa_open.screens import _object_html
270: 
271:     if paradigm.materials.kind != "svg":
272:         return []
273:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
274:     items: List[LegibilityItem] = []
275:     for domain in paradigm.materials.domains:
276:         base = _object_html(paradigm, domain, [], domain.name)
277:         items.append(LegibilityItem(f"{domain.name}: the base", "name",
278:                                     f"What is pictured? Name it in one or two words.\n{NAME_ASK}",
279:                                     row_png([base]), domain.name))
280:         words = [f.word for f in domain.features]
281:         for j, feature in enumerate(domain.features):
282:             order = [int(i) for i in rng.permutation(len(words))]
283:             shown = tuple(words[i] for i in order)
284:             listing = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}) {o}" for i, o in enumerate(shown))
285:             items.append(LegibilityItem(
286:                 f"{domain.name}: {feature.word}", "choice",
287:                 f"Object 2 is object 1 with one part added. Which word names the added part?\n{listing}\n{CHOICE_ASK}",
288:                 row_png([base, _object_html(paradigm, domain, [j], domain.name)]), feature.word, shown))
289:     if lists is not None:
290:         trials = [t for lst in lists["lists"] for t in lst["trials"] if t["phase"] == "test"]
291:         seen = set()
292:         for k in rng.permutation(len(trials)):
293:             t = trials[int(k)]
294:             n = len(t["objects"])
295:             mixed = [j for j in range(len(t["words"])) if 0 < sum(row[j] for row in t["objects"]) < n]
296:             key = (json.dumps(t["objects"]), t["domain"])
297:             if not mixed or key in seen:
298:                 continue
299:             seen.add(key)
300:             j = mixed[int(rng.integers(len(mixed)))]
301:             word = t["words"][j]
302:             having = {p + 1 for p, obj in enumerate(t["display_order"]) if t["objects"][obj][j]}
303:             items.append(LegibilityItem(
304:                 f"trial {len(seen)} ({t['domain_name']}): {word}", "truth",
305:                 f"The picture shows {n} objects, numbered 1 to {n} from left to right. Which of them have "
306:                 f"{word}?\n{TRUTH_ASK}", row_png(t["items_html"]), frozenset(having)))
307:             if len(seen) == TRUTH_ITEMS:
308:                 break
309:     return items
310: 
311: 
312: def _answer(reply: str) -> Optional[str]:
313:     found = ANSWER.findall(reply)
314:     return found[-1].strip().strip("`*").strip().rstrip(".") if found else None
315: 
316: 
317: def _judge_name(judge: Participant, given: str, intended: str) -> bool:
318:     reply = judge.reply(f"Someone shown a simple drawing named it \"{given}\". The drawing was meant to show one of "
319:                         f"the {intended}. Is \"{given}\" a reasonable name for that kind of thing (the same kind of "
320:                         f"object, a synonym, or a more specific kind)? Reply ANSWER: yes or ANSWER: no.")
321:     return (_answer(reply) or "").lower() == "yes"
322: 
323: 
324: def materials_check(paradigm, checkers: Sequence[Participant], out: Optional[Path] = None, *,
325:                     lists: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, judge: Optional[Participant] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
326:     """Each checker (a fresh chat) answers every legibility question; an item is misread when no
327:     more than half of them get it right: ``illegible`` for a feature or a trial, and
328:     ``unrecognised_bases`` (a warning) for a base. A free name that is not the domain's name
329:     (singular or plural) goes to ``judge`` (a fresh chat); without a judge it is wrong."""
330:     items = legibility_items(paradigm, lists)
331:     if not items:
332:         return {"items": 0, "legibility": None, "illegible": [], "unrecognised_bases": []}
333:     given: Dict[str, List[Optional[str]]] = {it.key: [] for it in items}
334:     right: Dict[str, List[bool]] = {it.key: [] for it in items}
335:     for c, checker in enumerate(checkers):
336:         transcript = []
337:         for it in items:
338:             reply = checker.reply(it.text, [it.image])
339:             transcript += [f"## {it.key}\n\n{it.text}", f"## Reply\n\n{reply}"]
340:             a = _answer(reply)
341:             if it.kind == "name":
342:                 ok = a is not None and (_plural_key(a) == _plural_key(it.expected) or
343:                                         (judge is not None and _judge_name(judge, a, it.expected)))
344:                 shown = a
345:             elif it.kind == "choice":
346:                 try:
347:                     k = int(a) - 1 if a is not None else -1
348:                 except ValueError:
349:                     k = -1
350:                 shown = it.options[k] if 0 <= k < len(it.options) else a
351:                 ok = shown == it.expected
352:             else:
353:                 nums = set()
354:                 if a is not None and a.lower() != "none":
355:                     try:
356:                         nums = {int(x) for x in re.split(r"[,\s]+", a) if x}
357:                     except ValueError:
358:                         nums = {-1}
359:                 shown = ", ".join(map(str, sorted(nums))) or "none"
360:                 ok = nums == set(it.expected)
361:             given[it.key].append(shown)
362:             right[it.key].append(ok)
363:         if out is not None:
364:             (out / "legibility").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
365:             (out / "legibility" / f"checker_{c}.md").write_text("\n\n".join(transcript))
366:     rows = []
367:     for it in items:
368:         expected = (", ".join(map(str, sorted(it.expected))) or "none") if it.kind == "truth" else it.expected
369:         rows.append({"item": it.key, "kind": it.kind, "right": sum(right[it.key]), "of": len(right[it.key]),
370:                      "answer": expected,
371:                      "wrong_answers": sorted({g for g, ok in zip(given[it.key], right[it.key]) if not ok and g})})
372:     total = sum(r["of"] for r in rows)
373:     misread = [r for r in rows if r["right"] * 2 <= r["of"]]
374:     return {"items": len(items), "legibility": sum(r["right"] for r in rows) / total,
375:             "illegible": [r for r in misread if r["kind"] != "name"],
376:             "unrecognised_bases": [r for r in misread if r["kind"] == "name"], "by_item": rows}
377: 
378: 
379: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- one participant
380: 
381: @dataclass
382: class Session:
383:     list_index: int
384:     checks: List[List[bool]] = field(default_factory=list)  # per reading of the instructions
385:     rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
386:     transcript: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
387: 
388: 
389: def _ask(participant: Participant, session: Session, text: str, images: Sequence[bytes] = ()) -> str:
390:     session.transcript.append(f"## Screen\n\n{text}" + (f"\n\n[{len(images)} image]" if images else ""))
391:     reply = participant.reply(text, images)
392:     session.transcript.append(f"## Reply\n\n{reply}")
393:     return reply
394: 
395: 
396: def _check(participant: Participant, session: Session, check: Mapping[str, Any], prefix: str) -> bool:
397:     options = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}) {o}" for i, o in enumerate(check["options"]))
398:     text = f"{prefix}{check['question']}\n{options}\nReply ANSWER: <the option's number>."
399:     found = ANSWER.findall(_ask(participant, session, text))
400:     try:
401:         return bool(found) and int(found[-1].strip().strip("`*").rstrip(".")) - 1 == check["correct"]
402:     except ValueError:
403:         return False
404: 
405: 
406: def run_participant(lists: Mapping[str, Any], index: int, participant: Participant) -> Session:
407:     lst = lists["lists"][index]
408:     intro, kind = lists["intro"], lists["materials_kind"]
409:     session = Session(index)
410:     lead = (f"Welcome. {intro['welcome']}\nIt takes about {lists['minutes']} minutes.\n\n"
411:             f"Instructions:\n{intro['task']}\n\n")
412:     for reading in range(2):
413:         answers = []
414:         for i, check in enumerate(intro["checks"]):
415:             prefix = lead if i == 0 else ""
416:             answers.append(_check(participant, session, check, prefix))
417:         session.checks.append(answers)
418:         if all(answers):
419:             break
420:         lead = f"Not quite: please read the instructions again.\n\nInstructions:\n{intro['task']}\n\n"
421:     for trial in lst["trials"]:
422:         text, images = trial_screen(trial, kind)
423:         response, why = parse_answer(trial, _ask(participant, session, text, images))
424:         if response is None:
425:             response, why = parse_answer(trial, _ask(
426:                 participant, session, f"Your answer could not be read: {why}. Please answer again.\n\n{text}", images))
427:         session.rows.append({"phase": trial["phase"], "unit": trial["unit"], "trial_number": trial["trial_number"],
428:                              "objects": trial["objects"], "heard": trial["heard"], "expect": trial.get("expect"),
429:                              **{k: trial[k] for k in ("probe", "target", "utterance") if k in trial},
430:                              "response": response, "unreadable": why if response is None else None})
431:     return session
432: 
433: 
434: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- the gate
435: 
436: def _records(timing: Optional[Sequence]) -> Sequence:
437:     from src.rsa_open.timing import CLOSED_CAMPAIGN
438: 
439:     return CLOSED_CAMPAIGN if timing is None else timing
440: 
441: 
442: def estimated_minutes(lists: Mapping[str, Any], timing: Optional[Sequence] = None) -> float:
443:     """A participant's minutes under these lists, calibrated on ``timing`` records (default: the
444:     closed campaign's; `src.rsa_open.timing.estimate`)."""
445:     from src.rsa_open.timing import estimate
446: 
447:     return estimate(lists, _records(timing))["estimated_minutes"]
448: 
449: 
450: def gate(paradigm, lists: Mapping[str, Any], sessions: Sequence[Session],
451:          timing: Optional[Sequence] = None, legibility: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
452:     from src.rsa_open.fit import OpenData
453:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import paradigm_likelihood
454:     from src.rsa_open.screens import catch_passed, scenes_and_responses
455: 
456:     rows = [r for s in sessions for r in s.rows]
457:     readable = [r for r in rows if r["response"] is not None]
458:     catches = [r for r in readable if r["phase"] == "catch"]
459:     n_catch = sum(r["phase"] == "catch" for r in rows)
460:     report: Dict[str, Any] = {
461:         "paradigm_sha256": paradigm.sha256, "design_sha256": lists["design_sha256"],
462:         "n_participants": len(sessions),
463:         "comprehension_first": sum(all(s.checks[0]) for s in sessions) / len(sessions),
464:         "comprehension_final": sum(all(s.checks[-1]) for s in sessions) / len(sessions),
465:         "catch_pass": sum(catch_passed(r) for r in catches) / max(n_catch, 1),
466:         "practice_pass": (sum(catch_passed(r) for r in readable if r["phase"] == "practice")
467:                           / max(sum(r["phase"] == "practice" for r in rows), 1)),
468:         "readable": len(readable) / max(len(rows), 1),
469:         "unreadable_examples": [r["unreadable"] for r in rows if r["response"] is None][:5],
470:         "declared_minutes": paradigm.design.minutes,
471:     }
472:     from src.rsa_open.timing import estimate
473: 
474:     t = estimate(lists, _records(timing))
475:     report.update(estimated_minutes=t["estimated_minutes"], time_model_minutes=t["model_minutes"],
476:                   time_calibration=t["calibration"], time_calibration_basis=t["calibration_basis"])
477:     if legibility is not None:
478:         report["legibility"] = legibility
479:     problems, warnings = [], []
480:     if report["comprehension_final"] < FLOORS["comprehension"]:
481:         problems.append(f"comprehension: {report['comprehension_final']:.0%} answered every check right by the "
482:                         f"second reading (floor {FLOORS['comprehension']:.0%})")
483:     if report["catch_pass"] < FLOORS["catch"]:
484:         problems.append(f"attention: {report['catch_pass']:.0%} of catch trials passed (floor {FLOORS['catch']:.0%})")
485:     if report["readable"] < FLOORS["readable"]:
486:         problems.append(f"readability: {report['readable']:.0%} of trials got a usable answer "
487:                         f"(floor {FLOORS['readable']:.0%}); e.g. {report['unreadable_examples'][:2]}")
488:     tests = [r for r in readable if r["phase"] == "test"]
489:     try:
490:         scenes, responses = scenes_and_responses(tests)
491:         OpenData.build(scenes, responses, paradigm_likelihood(paradigm))
492:         report["data_parse"] = "ok"
493:     except ValueError as err:
494:         report["data_parse"] = str(err)
495:         problems.append(f"data: the test responses do not parse as the link's data ({err})")
496:     ratio = report["estimated_minutes"] / paradigm.design.minutes
497:     report["time_ratio"] = ratio
498:     if abs(ratio - 1.0) > TIME_TOLERANCE:
499:         problems.append(f"time: estimated {report['estimated_minutes']:.1f} minutes against the declared "
500:                         f"{paradigm.design.minutes:g} (more than {TIME_TOLERANCE:.0%} apart): change the trials or "
501:                         f"the minutes (and the pay)")
502:     if legibility is not None and legibility["legibility"] is not None:
503:         bad = "; ".join(f"{r['item']} ({r['right']} of {r['of']} chose '{r['answer']}'"
504:                         + (f"; others chose {', '.join(r['wrong_answers'])}" if r["wrong_answers"] else "") + ")"
505:                         for r in legibility["illegible"])
506:         bases = "; ".join(f"the base of {r['item'].split(':')[0]} was not recognised ({r['right']} of {r['of']} "
507:                           f"named it '{r['answer']}' or a fair synonym"
508:                           + (f"; others said {', '.join(r['wrong_answers'])}" if r["wrong_answers"] else "") + ")"
509:                           for r in legibility.get("unrecognised_bases", []))
510:         if legibility["legibility"] < FLOORS["legibility"] or legibility["illegible"]:
511:             problems.append(f"legibility: {legibility['legibility']:.0%} of the materials questions answered right "
512:                             f"(floor {FLOORS['legibility']:.0%})" + (f"; misread: {bad}" if bad else "")
513:                             + (f"; {bases}" if bases else ""))
514:         elif bases:
515:             warnings.append(f"legibility: {bases}")
516:     distinct = {json.dumps(r["response"], sort_keys=True) for r in tests}
517:     if len(tests) > 1 and len(distinct) == 1:
518:         problems.append(f"degenerate: every test answer was {distinct.pop()}")
519:     report["problems"] = problems
520:     report["warnings"] = warnings
521:     report["passed"] = not problems
522:     return report
523: 
524: 
525: def run_pilot(paradigm, lists: Mapping[str, Any], out: Path, *, n_participants: int = PILOT_PARTICIPANTS,
526:               participant_factory: Optional[Callable[[int], Participant]] = None,
527:               max_workers: int = 6, timing: Optional[Sequence] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
528:     """Pilot ``n_participants`` lists (the first ones) and gate the paradigm; writes the record to ``out``."""
529:     if lists["paradigm_sha256"] != paradigm.sha256:
530:         raise ValueError("the lists were not built from this paradigm")
531:     n = min(n_participants, len(lists["lists"]))
532:     factory = participant_factory or (lambda i: GeminiParticipant())
533:     participants = [factory(i) for i in range(n)]
534:     with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool:
535:         sessions = list(pool.map(lambda i: run_participant(lists, i, participants[i]), range(n)))
536:     out = Path(out)
537:     # The materials check: fresh chats, so no participant's trials colour it.
538:     legibility = materials_check(paradigm, [factory(n + c) for c in range(LEGIBILITY_CHECKERS)], out, lists=lists,
539:                                  judge=factory(n + LEGIBILITY_CHECKERS))
540:     (out / "transcripts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
541:     for s in sessions:
542:         (out / "transcripts" / f"participant_{s.list_index:03d}.md").write_text("\n\n".join(s.transcript))
543:     with (out / "rows.jsonl").open("w") as f:
544:         for s in sessions:
545:             for r in s.rows:
546:                 f.write(json.dumps({"list_index": s.list_index, **r}) + "\n")
547:     report = gate(paradigm, lists, sessions, timing, legibility)
548:     report["participant_model"] = participants[0].name
549:     (out / "pilot.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
550:     return report
551: 
552: 
553: @dataclass
554: class Args:
555:     paradigm: Path
556:     lists: Path
557:     out: Path
558:     n_participants: int = PILOT_PARTICIPANTS
559: 
560: 
561: def main(args: Args) -> Dict[str, Any]:
562:     from src.rsa_open.paradigm import load_paradigm
563: 
564:     report = run_pilot(load_paradigm(args.paradigm), json.loads(args.lists.read_text()), args.out,
565:                        n_participants=args.n_participants)
566:     print(f"pilot {'PASSED' if report['passed'] else 'FAILED'}: " + ("; ".join(report["problems"]) or "no problems"))
567:     return report
568: 
569: 
570: if __name__ == "__main__":
571:     main(tyro.cli(Args))
